acceptance.given: The published policy and schemas, reference package, and normative standard are available as Package A validation inputs.

oracle.expected: Terminal validation evidence shows the actual published policy and schemas validate the reference package, and external review covers the normative standard.
forbidden: Unused or unpublished policy or schemas are substituted.
The reference package is not validated against the actual policy and schemas.
External review of the normative standard is omitted.
oracle.observable: Structured terminal evidence identifies the published policy and schema paths, validates the reference package, and records external review of docs/standards/skill-authoring-standard.md.

acceptance.then: The clean-validation evidence identifies the published inputs and reference package, and separate evidence identifies external review of the normative standard.
acceptance.when: Execute the declared Package A terminal pytest command and inspect its structured CLI and integration evidence.

affected_subjects: Clean package validation and standard review
slice_hint.behavior_change: Package A terminal validation must exercise the published policy and schemas against the reference package and require externally reviewable evidence for the normative standard.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing skill-contract and skill-input-contract protocols; revert only Package A validator, policy/schema, standard, and ADR/index changes if the contract cannot be demonstrated.

slice_hint.state_transition: From unpublished or insufficiently checked Package A inputs to validated published inputs, a passing reference package, and externally reviewed normative standard evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The declared migration, core, examples, and capabilities pytest modules pass; migration invokes the published CLI with literal argv, shell=False, repository cwd, and finite timeout; parses the versioned result with authorizes=[]; proves the reference package passes and a mutated package is rejected; and external-review evidence identifies the normative standard.
